args.user_asks: “Wait—stop talking. Do that instead, and when you’re done tell me where we left off.” (The pendant must interrupt speech immediately, redirect the active Mac/browser work, and later resume with a one-sentence checkpoint.)
args.why_useful: A wearable assistant is only trustworthy if the owner can change their mind mid-sentence without waiting for playback to finish or losing a multi-step task. This makes interruption, redirection, and recovery one natural voice interaction across all surfaces.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for barge-in intent and a short acknowledgement; background planner on the cheaper local Mac model for checkpointing and redirected work.
args.latency_budget: Mute/acknowledge within 250 ms of detected speech; redirect dispatch within 2 s; completion notification when the existing job receipt is available.
args.cost_estimate: Low incremental API cost: one short realtime turn per interruption; checkpoint and planning use local Mac inference. Dominant cost is audio streaming, not reasoning.
args.security_concerns: The spoken interruption and current task state cross the relay; browser credentials remain in the authenticated Mac bridge. Redirecting an irreversible action must still stop at the existing approval checkpoint.
missing: firmware barge-in VAD and an immediate playback mute signal
a resumable task checkpoint schema that can be replaced by a spoken redirect
relay cancellation/redirect semantics that preserve the old receipt and link the new one

args.user_asks: “Save this moment so I can find it later.” The system should bind what I just said to the active Safari page, selected text, visible screen evidence, and the resulting task or reminder, then let me retrieve it by natural language.
args.why_useful: People lose the connection between a thought and the page that caused it. A wearable trigger plus browser provenance creates a searchable memory with evidence instead of an ungrounded transcript or a bookmark that lacks intent.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the short capture command; local Mac vision/browser extraction for page and selection evidence; cheap background model for normalization and later retrieval.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge capture in under 500 ms; gather page/selection/screenshot evidence within 5 s; retrieval answer under 3 s when indexed.
args.cost_estimate: Usually one short realtime turn plus local OCR/extraction. Storage is small JSON plus optional compressed screenshot; screenshot retention dominates storage, not API calls.
args.security_concerns: Private page content and screenshots must stay on the Mac by default, with only hashes/structured snippets sent to relay. Mask passwords/payment fields and require explicit confirmation before syncing sensitive evidence.
missing: a unified moment-record route joining audio transcript, active tab, selection, screenshot and action receipt
Mac active-window/selection capture that works without Accessibility where possible
natural-language retrieval over moment records with per-field sensitivity filtering

args.user_asks: “My pendant is silent—fix it.” The system should test the entire worn-audio chain, identify whether the fault is USB, firmware, relay, Opus, I2S, ESP32, or headphones, repair safe software faults, and tell me exactly what I need to reconnect or approve.
args.why_useful: Today a silent wearable can fail at several opaque boundaries. One voice command should turn a frustrating hardware hunt into a bounded diagnosis, using the Mac as a serial instrument and the relay as the end-to-end observer.
args.model_tier: Cheap deterministic diagnostics first; local planner interprets logs and chooses safe retries; realtime model only explains the result conversationally.
args.latency_budget: First fault hypothesis in 10 s; safe retries within 30 s; never claim recovery until a loopback/test tone and receipt confirm it.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for scripted probes; occasional local planner call. USB serial tests and generated test audio dominate elapsed time.
args.security_concerns: Firmware flashing, deleting recordings, or changing Bluetooth pairing require explicit confirmation. Diagnostics may contain transcripts and device identifiers; retain only a redacted receipt.
missing: a Mac serial diagnostic tool for /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
end-to-end synthetic audio correlation IDs across pendant, relay, and bridge
a safe repair matrix and human-readable fault receipt

args.change: Add a USB-serial companion transport that makes the physically connected nRF9160 and ESP32 a first-class local pendant path when LTE is unregistered: framed, authenticated audio/events over /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, with the same correlation IDs and receipts as relay traffic. The relay chooses LTE or Mac-USB per session, never both, and the pendant LED reports which path is active.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear and test the real pendant today instead of waiting for cellular registration; conversations, playback, and button events continue over the Mac while preserving the same behavior they will get away from home.
args.effort: Medium: Mac serial daemon, Zephyr framing/transport adapter, ESP32 bridge routing, relay session-path selection, and an end-to-end test harness.
args.risk: USB disconnects or partial frames could wedge audio; use sequence numbers, bounded buffers, watchdog reset, and automatic fallback to LTE. Never silently route microphone audio over USB without the session LED state and dashboard indicator.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; roughly 1–2 weeks engineering. No hardware cost; Mac CPU/USB power is minor.
args.latency_impact: Potentially lower latency than LTE (USB transport), with one extra framing hop; reconnect should be under 2 s.
args.security_impact: USB is a local trust boundary, not inherently private: authenticate the companion handshake, reject unknown serial identities, and encrypt audio/control frames if the Mac daemon is not the signed app.
depends_on: Mac serial diagnostic/access tool for both live device paths
stable audio packet framing and correlation IDs shared with /pipeline/audio
relay session transport selection and duplicate suppression

transcript.text:
Round 122 produced four new proposals:

1. **Interruptible, redirectable work** — say “stop talking; do this instead,” immediately mute the pendant, redirect the active Mac/browser job, preserve the old receipt, and later report where the work resumed.
2. **Evidence-backed moment capture** — “save this moment” binds the spoken thought to the active Safari page, selected text, screen evidence, and resulting task/reminder, with privacy filtering.
3. **End-to-end “fix my silent pendant” diagnosis** — test USB, firmware, relay, Opus, I²S, ESP32, and headphones; perform only safe repairs; provide a fault receipt.
4. **USB-local pendant mode** — because both chips are physically connected now, use the Mac as a transport fallback while LTE is unregistered, with the same correlation IDs, receipts, and LED path indication as relay sessions.

What is still needed:

- A Mac serial companion for the two live device paths.
- Shared audio/event correlation IDs and duplicate suppression across USB and LTE.
- Firmware barge-in detection and immediate playback mute.
- A unified “moment” record and retrieval path with sensitive-field filtering.
- A resumable task checkpoint/redirect protocol.
- Deterministic audio-chain diagnostic probes and a safe repair matrix.
- Owner decisions on privacy boundaries for screenshots, microphone audio, and USB companion routing.

The most important gap is **reliable interruption and continuation**: without it, a wearable conversation still feels like a one-shot voice command rather than an assistant that can work alongside the owner.

args.user_asks: “Lock everything down now.” The pendant should immediately mute its microphone and playback, pause queued Mac/browser work, revoke active browser sessions, disable new actions, and give me a short spoken confirmation; I can later say “restore” to re-enable only the devices and jobs I approve.
args.why_useful: A lost pendant, exposed screen, or mistaken command can otherwise leave several surfaces active at once. One physical/voice emergency command gives the owner a clear, reversible digital firebreak across the wearable, relay, Mac, and private browser.
args.model_tier: Deterministic control plane only for lock, pause, revoke, and confirmation; no expensive model should be needed. Use the realtime model only if the owner asks for an explanation afterward.
args.latency_budget: Local mute and button acknowledgement under 150 ms; relay-wide lock under 2 s; all active jobs visibly marked locked within 5 s.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero API cost. Dominant work is implementing revocation and reliable propagation across the four surfaces.
args.security_concerns: The lock command must be accepted from a physical button gesture even if the network is unavailable, and must not be bypassable by an already-running job. Restore requires explicit physical confirmation or a pre-authorized recovery phrase; preserve audit receipts without retaining microphone audio.
missing: a durable fleet-wide emergency-lock state with monotonic generation numbers
firmware-local microphone/playback mute latch and a distinct unlock gesture
Mac and browser agents that check the lock generation before every action and revoke authenticated browser sessions
a recovery UI showing exactly what is paused, revoked, or still unreachable

args.user_asks: “Show me exactly what would happen if I did that, but don’t change anything.” The system should run a cross-surface dry run—browser form effects, Mac file/calendar/mail effects, and downstream job changes—then present a before/after diff without touching the real accounts or filesystem.
args.why_useful: The owner can safely explore consequential workflows instead of choosing between blind trust and manually checking every surface. It is especially valuable when one request crosses a logged-in browser and local Mac state.
args.model_tier: Local Mac planner and deterministic adapters perform the simulation; a cheap model summarizes the diff. Realtime is used only to acknowledge and read back a concise result.
args.latency_budget: Preview acknowledgement under 1 s; simple previews under 10 s; complex multi-surface previews may take 30 s but must show progress.
args.cost_estimate: Low-to-moderate local compute; API cost is one summary call. Storage cost is temporary isolated browser profiles and filesystem snapshots.
args.security_concerns: Simulation must use isolated browser sessions, shadow files, and non-sending mail/calendar APIs. If an adapter cannot guarantee dry-run semantics, mark that operation “not simulated” rather than execute it. Never upload private page contents merely to generate the diff.
missing: transactional dry-run adapters for AppleScript, filesystem, browser forms, and job scheduling
isolated browser/session and temporary Mac workspace snapshots
a typed cross-surface before/after diff format with unsimulated-operation warnings

args.change: Add a low-power haptic actuator and a second tactile control to the production pendant, with a local event vocabulary: short pulse for listening, double pulse for approval needed, long pulse for completion/error, and a hold gesture for the emergency lock. Keep the existing LED/button compatibility for the prototype and expose the same events to relay receipts.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can understand and control the assistant discreetly in public, in darkness, or when headphones are disconnected—without looking at a screen or speaking sensitive commands aloud. The emergency gesture also works when the network is down.
args.effort: Production enclosure/PCB revision, GPIO or I2C driver, firmware event mapping, and accessibility testing; prototype validation can use an external haptic breakout on the currently free I2C/GPIO resources.
args.risk: False holds or vibration fatigue could annoy the owner; require deliberate timing, configurable patterns, and a physical override. Added openings and wiring need water/impact testing.
args.cost_impact: Approximately $2–6 BOM increase plus PCB/enclosure revision; haptic draw is tens of milliamps only during brief pulses, with negligible daily energy impact.
args.latency_impact: Local feedback is immediate (<50 ms) and removes reliance on network round trips for confirmation.
args.security_impact: A physical lock gesture reduces remote misuse, but unlock must require a distinct long hold plus spoken or dashboard confirmation; never expose raw gesture events as authority without replay protection.
depends_on: firmware-local mute/lock latch
event correlation and receipt protocol shared with relay
production pendant design replacing the current provisional nRF9160 DK enclosure

transcript.text:
Recorded three additional items:

- **Fleet-wide emergency lock:** a physical/voice “lock everything down” command that mutes the pendant, pauses jobs, revokes browser sessions, blocks new actions, and supports explicit recovery.
- **Cross-surface dry-run previews:** “show me what would happen” without modifying browser accounts, Mac files, calendars, or jobs, with a typed before/after diff and warnings for anything that cannot be simulated.
- **Production pendant haptics and a second control:** discreet local feedback and an offline emergency-lock gesture, so the owner can operate the assistant without speech, a screen, or headphones.

They require, respectively:

- A durable lock generation checked by every agent, local firmware mute/lock behavior, browser-session revocation, and recovery UI.
- True transactional dry-run adapters, isolated browser sessions and Mac workspaces, and a cross-surface diff format.
- A production pendant PCB/enclosure revision, haptic driver, second sealed control, local gesture handling, and shared event receipts.

args.user_asks: “Make the pendant work as my voice terminal even when LTE is unavailable.”
args.why_useful: This is the most immediately valuable missing behavior: the physically connected nRF9160 and ESP32 can be used today over USB, so the owner gets live voice instead of a dead wearable while LTE registration is absent. When LTE returns, the same conversation should continue without restarting.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the live conversation; a cheap background worker records the handoff and reconciliation receipt.
args.latency_budget: Local USB fallback should begin within 300 ms and keep round-trip conversational latency under 700 ms; LTE transition may take up to 2 s with no lost committed turn.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible incremental model cost; local USB audio dominates. A fallback turn costs the same realtime inference as today, while health probes are sub-cent.
args.security_concerns: USB audio and transcripts remain on the owner's Mac unless the live relay is explicitly selected. Never silently upload buffered offline speech; announce link mode and require confirmation before sending queued audio or actions.
missing: A USB-serial audio/control adapter for the Mac harness
A relay session handoff protocol with sequence numbers and duplicate suppression
A pendant-visible link-mode indicator and reconnect state machine
End-to-end acceptance test with LTE absent, then restored

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: All 7 pieces you named already exist: /pipeline/audio, /pipeline/events, /pipeline, /browser/status, /execute, /jobs/:jobid/receipts. So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.user_asks: “Move this conversation to my Mac, use my logged-in browser if needed, and let me pick it back up on the pendant.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is ideal for speaking and interruption, while the Mac/browser are the only surfaces that can inspect private pages and perform multi-step work. A resumable handoff would make the hive feel like one assistant rather than disconnected agents.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for the short handoff utterance; background/local planner handles browser work and writes a compact checkpoint.
args.latency_budget: A handoff receipt in under 1 s; resume should speak the current state in one short sentence within 2 s. Long browser work runs asynchronously.
args.cost_estimate: One small realtime turn plus cheap planner calls; checkpoint storage is tiny and dominates neither latency nor cost.
args.security_concerns: The checkpoint must include tab/session IDs but not page secrets or full private content. Browser actions remain reversible/draft-first, and any send/purchase requires the existing confirmation policy.
missing: Cross-surface conversation checkpoint schema with expiry
Session-bound browser context reattachment and spoken resume event
A pendant gesture/phrase to resume the latest checkpoint
Unified receipt linking relay, Mac job, and browser command IDs

args.user_asks: “When I’m interrupted, save exactly where we were and bring me back up to speed when I tap the pendant.”
args.why_useful: Real wearable use is fragmented. A durable, privacy-scoped interruption card would preserve the last question, pending decision, evidence links, and unfinished action, then give a concise spoken catch-up without replaying or repeating work.
args.model_tier: Cheap background summarization creates the card; realtime is used only to deliver the short spoken catch-up or clarify a decision.
args.latency_budget: Capture in under 500 ms on disconnect/button press; catch-up audio starts within 1 s after resume.
args.cost_estimate: A few hundred tokens per interruption card; no extra inference on ordinary uninterrupted turns.
args.security_concerns: Cards need TTL, encryption, and sensitivity labels. Do not store raw microphone audio by default; private browser snippets should be represented by citations and hashes, not copied content. Destructive pending actions must be clearly marked and never auto-resumed.
missing: Disconnect/button event ingestion from the pendant
A compact checkpoint store with TTL and sensitivity filtering
Resume speech protocol and idempotent action status lookup
Owner-facing list of active interruption cards

args.change: Add a USB-local pendant transport beside LTE: a Mac daemon opens /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, packetizes the existing Opus frames with a monotonically increasing session/sequence header, and exposes the same pipeline audio/events contract. The relay chooses USB or LTE per measured heartbeat and performs a two-phase handoff (stop accepting old path, replay only missing sequence numbers, then resume).
args.why_useful_to_owner: Their wearable remains usable today while physically tethered to the Mac and can move back to LTE later without restarting a conversation or duplicating speech.
args.effort: Medium-high: Mac serial daemon, pendant framing changes, relay state machine, and hardware-in-loop tests.
args.risk: A bad handoff could duplicate audio or strand a session; recover by keeping a short jitter/replay window and falling back to the last healthy path. No automatic upload of queued audio.
args.cost_impact: No model-cost change; one small always-on Mac process and modest serial CPU.
args.latency_impact: USB path should be faster than LTE; handoff adds up to 2 seconds only during transition.
args.security_impact: Treat USB as local trusted transport, authenticate the daemon with a per-install key, and visibly announce whether audio is local or remote.
depends_on: A USB-serial adapter implementation
Sequence-aware relay session handoff

transcript.summary:
This round produced three owner-facing advances: (1) a cross-surface “safety check this” gate that scans drafts for secrets, wrong recipients, stale facts, and irreversible consequences before approval; (2) a pendant-local “stop everything” kill switch that mutes audio and cancels/freeze Mac and browser work even during link degradation; and (3) failure-aware recovery that explains the exact failed step, preserves evidence, and offers a safe alternate route rather than blindly replaying. I also proposed an end-to-end audio clock governor and physical acceptance harness for the live nRF9160 + ESP32 prototype, so long 24 kHz sessions do not drift or silently drop speech.

What I still need is implementation, not another discovery round: the cross-surface evidence/redaction scanner; a firmware stop latch plus relay-wide idempotent cancellation and resume checkpoints; normalized partial-progress/error receipts; and the serial audio telemetry, ESP32 adaptive resampler, and acceptance fixture. The pending audio validation/threshold decisions remain the main product unknown. The connected chips are testable over USB today, but the pendant is still not LTE-registered, so network-independent stop and diagnostics must be exercised first.
transcript.biggest_unknown: Whether the current physical audio path can meet intelligibility and dropout thresholds under simultaneous Opus encode/decode and SBC Bluetooth load; no live acceptance measurement has established that yet.

args.user_asks: “Mark this moment.” While I’m speaking, have the pendant create a durable, timestamped marker; the Mac captures the active app/window and authenticated browser tab, the relay stores the audio/transcript and provenance, and later I can ask “what was that moment?” to retrieve the exact context and continue the task.
args.why_useful: A single button press turns fleeting thoughts, decisions, or meeting moments into a retrievable evidence bundle. No other node can know both the physical instant and the private screen state; together they can.
args.model_tier: background for transcription/indexing; realtime only for the immediate spoken acknowledgement
args.latency_budget: LED acknowledgement under 150 ms; marker receipt under 3 s; indexing may finish in the background
args.cost_estimate: ~$0.01–$0.05 per marker depending on transcription length; storage dominates only for retained audio
args.security_concerns: Audio and private tab metadata leave the device to the authenticated relay; redact secrets and page bodies by default, retain source hashes and require confirmation before sharing a marker. Button gesture must be unambiguous.
missing: pendant marker gesture and bounded local buffer
Mac active-window and browser-tab snapshot API
relay marker index with audio/transcript retention policy
spoken/dashboard retrieval by time, project, or quoted phrase

args.change: Add a local “moment marker” state machine to the pendant: a long press snapshots the last 8 seconds of encoded mic frames into a bounded ring, emits one framed marker event over the existing USB/UART or LTE transport with monotonic timestamp and sequence number, then immediately resumes live audio. The relay acknowledges receipt and the Mac/browser collectors attach current context asynchronously; never block the audio thread or attempt transcription on the nRF9160.
args.why_useful_to_owner: They can capture a decision or insight even when the conversation moves too quickly to repeat it, and the marker survives a dropped link long enough to be indexed when the Mac reconnects.
args.effort: Medium firmware plus relay event schema and a small Mac context collector; test ring-buffer overwrite, button bounce, reconnect, and power loss.
args.risk: A stuck button or noisy UART could create repeated markers; debounce, one-marker-per-press, sequence deduplication, and a visible LED pattern recover safely. The ring is intentionally bounded so it cannot fill RAM.
args.cost_impact: No per-use model cost on-device; roughly 8–20 kB RAM/flash depending on frame duration and metadata. Relay transcription/storage costs apply only when the owner retains a marker.
args.latency_impact: <150 ms local LED/event acknowledgement; context attachment and transcription are asynchronous and may take seconds.
args.security_impact: Local audio is retained briefly only in volatile memory; relay must encrypt markers, apply short default retention, and omit page contents unless explicitly requested.
depends_on: a marker event contract between firmware, relay, Mac, and browser
a retrieval surface for marker provenance

args.why_useful: It lets the owner leave the desk without losing the exact private webpage they were reading. Browser authentication supplies access, the Mac supplies the bridge, and the worn device supplies an interruption-free listening and control surface.

args.security_concerns: Read only the active authenticated tab and explicitly exclude password inputs, tokens, and editable form controls. Keep source URL and citation private; require confirmation if the page contains a sensitive category or if any action beyond reading is requested.

a durable audio queue shared by relay and Mac

transcript.summary: This round produced three new cross-surface owner capabilities and one implementable firmware change. The strongest is “Mark this moment”: a long press captures a bounded recent audio window, while the Mac and authenticated browser snapshot active context and the relay makes the moment searchable with provenance. I also proposed browser-to-pendant page handoff with citations, and gesture-gated “Explain that” for meeting terms. The firmware change defines the local marker ring and non-blocking event protocol. Today the Mac bridge and Safari are online; the pendant is physically USB-connected but not LTE-registered, so USB-tether testing is the immediate path.
transcript.biggest_unknown: The end-to-end audio acceptance criteria and the exact Mac/browser APIs for active-window/tab snapshots remain unspecified. I still need those contracts, plus a durable marker/audio queue and retrieval surface; without them the proposals are connective designs rather than runnable owner experiences.

args.change: Replace the prototype pendant’s single-button/single-LED UI with a production interaction module: two tactile buttons plus a low-power haptic actuator and RGB status indicator, while retaining the existing I2S full-duplex audio and USB service path. Define distinct gestures for mark, private/mute, playback navigation, and approval; use haptics for acknowledgements and errors when audio output is unavailable or socially inappropriate.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can control and trust the assistant discreetly in a meeting, on a street, or with headphones disconnected. They no longer have to guess whether a long press registered from one ambiguous button and one tiny LED.
args.effort: High: industrial design, GPIO/I2C allocation, waterproof wearable enclosure, firmware gesture/accessibility work, and a production electrical redesign; validate accidental-press resistance and one-handed operation.
args.risk: More controls can cause accidental actions or confusion; require distinct press durations, haptic patterns, lockout after ambiguous gestures, and a spoken/visual configuration tutorial. If the haptic or RGB module fails, the current audio/LED path remains usable.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $3–$12 added BOM in small volume plus enclosure redesign; haptic pulses are tens of milliwatts and negligible relative to radio/audio peaks. No per-use API cost.
args.latency_impact: Local acknowledgement can be under 100 ms, substantially faster than relay confirmation; no network latency added.
args.security_impact: A dedicated private/mute control reduces accidental recording and output disclosure. Firmware must make privacy state fail-closed across reboot and visibly/haptically distinguish muted from active.
depends_on: production pendant constraints and enclosure design
a stable gesture/event contract shared with relay, Mac, and browser
local privacy and output-mute state semantics

transcript.text:
Recorded a new hardware proposal: a production pendant with two tactile buttons, haptic feedback, and an RGB indicator.

The owner should be able to control marking, privacy/mute, playback, and approvals discreetly—even when audio is unavailable or inappropriate. The current single-button/single-LED prototype cannot provide reliable, distinguishable feedback.

It would require a production enclosure and electrical redesign, new gesture semantics across pendant/Mac/browser/relay, and fail-closed privacy behavior across reboot. Estimated added hardware cost is roughly $3–$12 per unit, with negligible power impact.

args.user_asks: “Keep my conversation alive when I leave Wi‑Fi: if the pendant is plugged into my Mac over USB, switch the live call to that local link, then move it back to LTE when available without losing the transcript or repeating my request.”
args.why_useful: The pendant is physically testable over USB today but is not LTE-registered. This gives the owner one continuous wearable conversation instead of a dead device whenever cellular coverage or registration fails, while preserving exactly-once task execution across transport changes.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the active voice stream; a cheaper background model reconciles transcript segments and transport receipts after handoff.
args.latency_budget: Handoff under 2 seconds, with at most one replay-free audio gap; reconciliation can finish within 10 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible inference increase during handoff; roughly 1–2 extra short realtime turns per transport change. Dominant cost is persistent audio/WebSocket bandwidth, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: USB serial audio and control stay on the owner's Mac; relay must authenticate the pendant session and bind both transports to one nonce. Never duplicate an irreversible Mac/browser action when reconnecting; require the existing confirmation policy for destructive actions.

args.user_asks: “If I am in the middle of a browser or Mac task and the pendant disconnects, stop before any irreversible step, tell me exactly where you stopped, and resume only when I explicitly say ‘continue’.”
args.why_useful: A disconnected wearable can mean loss of attention, privacy, or transport. This turns a silent failure into a safe, inspectable pause, protecting the owner from a queued send, purchase, deletion, or navigation occurring after they can no longer hear the confirmation.
args.model_tier: Deterministic rules handle disconnect detection and checkpointing; a cheap model summarizes the paused state. Realtime is used only to announce the stop when a path remains available.
args.latency_budget: Pause within 250 ms of confirmed link loss; receipt available within 2 seconds of reconnection.
args.cost_estimate: No per-event model cost for the safety latch; one short summary call per paused job at most.
args.security_concerns: Default-deny for irreversible actions after disconnect, with idempotent cancellation and durable receipts. Do not expose private page contents in reconnect notifications until the pendant is authenticated again.

transcript.text:
Round 127 produced four proposals:

1. **Transport handoff for live conversations** — keep one conversation alive when switching between the pendant’s USB connection and LTE, with sequence numbers preventing duplicate actions.
2. **Explicit “save this moment” capture** — bind a short pendant audio marker to the active Mac window, Safari tab, transcript, and job evidence.
3. **Disconnect-safe task pausing** — immediately pause browser/Mac work before irreversible actions when the pendant disappears, then resume only after an explicit “continue.”
4. **Wearable link-test mode** — run a spoken end-to-end test through the USB-connected nRF9160 and ESP32, measuring latency, packet loss, underruns, drift, and output quality.

I also recorded two live truths:

- The boards are physically reachable over USB now, but the pendant is not LTE-registered.
- Owner memory says **America/Chicago**, while machine context says **America/New_York**. Scheduling and spoken times need an authoritative timezone decision.

What is still needed:

- A Mac USB-serial transport bridge for the pendant and ESP32.
- Transport migration and exactly-once action sequence handling.
- A disconnect heartbeat tied to active jobs, with a pre-irreversible-action checkpoint.
- A privacy-controlled moment-marker/audio spool and cross-surface evidence index.
- Firmware and bridge diagnostic counters for the audio test.
- Final 24 kHz audio acceptance thresholds.
- An authoritative timezone policy before any time-sensitive automation.

args.user_asks: “When I’m busy, let the pendant be my interruptibility switch: one gesture should put my Mac, browser, and relay into quiet mode, defer nonurgent work, and let only genuinely urgent events break through; another gesture restores normal operation.”
args.why_useful: Today quieting notifications, stopping background browser work, and changing wearable behavior are separate operations. A physical switch gives the owner an immediate, reliable boundary without opening an app or speaking over an interruption.
args.model_tier: Deterministic local state and relay policy; a cheap model classifies urgency only when an event is ambiguous.
args.latency_budget: Local gesture feedback under 150 ms; Mac/browser policy convergence under 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for explicit mode changes; occasional small classification calls for incoming events.
args.security_concerns: The mode must fail closed on disconnect and never suppress safety-critical alerts. Store only the mode and expiry, not ambient audio. Require an explicit gesture or spoken command to exit quiet mode.

args.user_asks: “If a private website logs me out or asks for a security check, tell me exactly what happened through the pendant, guide me to the right Safari tab, and wait while I complete the login—never handle or repeat my password or code.”

args.latency_budget: Detect and announce within 3 seconds; resume the waiting job within 5 seconds after a fresh authenticated heartbeat.
args.cost_estimate: No model call for ordinary detection; one short realtime turn for guidance and one background reconciliation after recovery.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner could change modes, approve or cancel actions, and receive private confirmations without speaking or looking at a screen—especially in meetings, outdoors, or when the pendant is under clothing.
args.effort: High: enclosure and industrial design, low-power driver, debounce/gesture firmware, interrupt routing, and an interaction vocabulary tested with real wear conditions.
args.risk: False gestures or hidden confirmations could cause confusion or unsafe actions. Require deliberate multi-step gestures for consequential actions, make haptic patterns distinguishable, and fall back to the physical button plus LED.
args.cost_impact: Roughly $3–8 in added components at production volume, with tens to hundreds of microwatts idle and brief milliwatt-level haptic pulses.
args.latency_impact: Local feedback can be sub-100 ms; no network latency added.
args.security_impact: Enables private local confirmation, reducing spoken leakage. Sensor data should remain local and expose only coarse state, not raw proximity traces.

transcript.text:
Recorded four new proposals:

- A physical **interruptibility switch** spanning pendant, Mac, browser, and relay.
- **Browser authentication recovery** that guides the owner through expired sessions without exposing credentials.
- **Verified end-state receipts** that compare before/after reality instead of trusting action success responses.
- A production **private interaction module** with haptics and deliberate gestures.

They require, respectively:

- Shared interruptibility state and pendant gesture events.
- Typed browser auth-challenge results and a secure paused-job state.
- Cross-surface before/after snapshots and a verification stage.
- New pendant hardware, firmware gesture handling, and a tested tactile vocabulary.

All four were passed to the proposal recorder.

pendant.flash: 1 MB total; application text ~316 kB with libopus at -O3

io.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
io.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
io.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.
io.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.

storage.sd: microSD over SPI. CONFIG_DISK_DRIVER_SDMMC, FATFS (ELM) with exFAT enabled. Mount is FS_FATFS.
storage.policy: Owner's standing rule: audio is written to SD ONLY when a chunk upload cannot be uploaded. It is a failure buffer, not a routine store.
storage.note: exFAT means large files and long filenames are available.

audio.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
audio.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
audio.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

bridge.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
bridge.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
bridge.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

network.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
network.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
network.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

stack.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
stack.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
stack.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
stack.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
stack.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
stack.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

power.supply: USB or battery. LTE-M transmit bursts draw far more than idle.
power.note: No battery gauge is wired up today, so the agent cannot read charge state.

result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on the owner's MacBook (unified). Every device described here is REMOTE to you — you are not running on the pendant or the ESP32.

args.user_asks: “Move this conversation to my Mac” (or back to the pendant) and keep going without repeating anything.”
args.why_useful: The owner can start hands-free while walking, then continue with a screen when the task becomes visual—or leave the Mac and keep the same thread in their ear. The worn device, Mac, browser, and relay each contribute a reach no single surface has.
args.model_tier: Realtime model handles only the brief handoff intent and spoken confirmation; a cheaper background model compiles the session state and summarizes browser/Mac evidence.
args.latency_budget: Acknowledge the migration in under 1 second; reconstruct the target surface in under 5 seconds. The owner tolerates a single spoken confirmation, not a repeated transcript.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.01–$0.05 per migration, dominated by the short realtime turn and background context summary; browser/Mac reads are local.
args.security_concerns: Only transfer the minimum session state, with private-tab content and audio excluded unless the owner explicitly says to include them. Never migrate a pending irreversible action; require confirmation again on the target surface.

A resumable audio/text cursor so migration does not replay or lose turns

args.model_tier: No expensive model is needed for failover: firmware and the Mac bridge detect link state and buffer frames; realtime is used only if the conversation itself needs a response.
args.latency_budget: Detect failure in under 500 ms, resume audio in under 2 seconds, and hide one reconnect blip from the owner. Preserve ordering and never replay a completed utterance.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero per invocation beyond ordinary realtime audio; engineering cost is firmware/USB transport and test coverage. A local fallback actually reduces paid relay calls when LTE is unavailable.
args.security_concerns: USB audio and transcripts stay on the owner's Mac unless the existing relay connection is healthy. Authenticate the serial peer, encrypt any persisted fallback buffer, cap retention, and visibly indicate local-only mode with the LED/dashboard.

transcript.text:
Recorded this round:

1. **Transparent LTE-to-USB fallback** — keep a conversation alive through the Mac when LTE drops, then resume LTE without replaying or losing speech.
2. **Cross-surface “what was I doing?” handoff** — spoken one-sentence resume point from active Mac/browser work.
3. **Selective attention monitoring** — watch an opted-in meeting or page and interrupt only when the owner needs to act.
4. **Firmware transport state machine** — sequence audio frames, detect link health, and support LTE↔USB handoff with duplicate suppression.

One proposed idea was rejected because it already exists: moving a live conversation between the pendant and Mac.

What is still needed:

- A framed, authenticated bidirectional USB audio/control protocol for `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*`.
- Relay session epochs, sequence numbers, and duplicate suppression for transport failover.
- Mac-side USB audio integration plus LTE↔USB fault-injection tests.
- A typed cross-surface session envelope containing provenance, sensitivity, freshness, and an audio/text cursor.
- An atomic attention snapshot covering active Mac app, browser tab, unfinished jobs, and resume point.
- An opt-in monitoring policy with urgency levels, quiet hours, deduplication, and spoken delivery receipts.

Current reality: the Mac bridge and Safari are online; the pendant is physically USB-connected and testable, but it is not LTE-registered.

args.user_asks: “Why did I decide this, and what evidence was I looking at?” Give me the short answer plus a timeline of the sources that led to the decision.
args.why_useful: The owner can recover the reasoning behind a choice made days ago instead of rereading tabs, messages, notes, and spoken conversations. The pendant supplies the question hands-free; the relay correlates time; the Mac and authenticated browser provide the private evidence; the dashboard shows citations and uncertainty.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to build and index an evidence timeline; use the realtime model only to answer the spoken question and summarize the already-ranked evidence.
args.latency_budget: A one-sentence answer within 5 seconds; a cited timeline within 15 seconds. If evidence conflicts, explicitly say so rather than inventing rationale.
args.cost_estimate: Approximately $0.02–$0.10 per recall, dominated by timeline retrieval and synthesis; local extraction and hashed indexes keep routine indexing inexpensive.
args.security_concerns: Only search sources the owner authorized, preserve source-level sensitivity labels, and never speak secrets aloud by default. Store citations and hashes rather than raw page content where possible; require confirmation before exposing sensitive evidence on the dashboard or pendant.
missing: A provenance-preserving decision ledger that links spoken captures, notes, browser observations, calendar context, and executed actions by time and session
A cross-surface retrieval API with source citations, confidence, and contradiction detection
An owner-facing retention and deletion control for the linked evidence trail

args.user_asks: “I need help now.” Have the pendant enter emergency mode, alert my chosen contacts with my location and a short live status, and keep me informed until I cancel it.
args.why_useful: A worn device is valuable precisely when the owner cannot reach a phone or screen. The pendant can provide a local trigger and voice channel, the relay stays awake, and the Mac/phone/browser can deliver the alert and location through services the pendant cannot reach alone.
args.model_tier: No large model should be in the critical path. Firmware and relay handle the trigger and delivery state machine; a small background model may compose a concise status message only after the emergency channel is established.
args.latency_budget: Local alarm and spoken acknowledgement immediately; contact notification within 10 seconds where network permits; retry and report delivery state rather than claiming success.
args.cost_estimate: Low API cost, roughly $0.01 or less per event; SMS/voice/location-provider fees and relay availability dominate.
args.security_concerns: Require a deliberate gesture or phrase plus a short cancellation window to reduce false alarms. Encrypt location, use an allowlisted contact set, expire sharing automatically, log delivery receipts, and never expose emergency data to ordinary browser or memory searches.
missing: A production emergency trigger and local confirmation path on the pendant
Location acquisition and a phone/relay delivery integration with provider failover

args.user_asks: “I lost my pendant.” Lock it immediately, revoke its credentials, show its last known connection, and preserve my unfinished work so I can continue safely on my Mac.
args.why_useful: A wearable contains microphones, recordings, network identity, and potentially sensitive cached audio. Today there is no owner-facing lost-device response. args.model_tier: This should be deterministic control-plane logic, not a model task. Use a small model only to summarize which sessions were affected after revocation.
args.latency_budget: Credential revocation and output lock within seconds; last-seen and affected-session report within 15 seconds. Recovery must work even if the pendant is offline.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost; storage and push-notification costs are minor. The major work is secure firmware and credential lifecycle design.
args.security_concerns: Use a separately authenticated recovery channel and a clearly named device identity. Revoke WebSocket credentials, invalidate queued commands, wipe or cryptographically forget SD failure buffers on next contact, and never reveal location beyond the owner’s devices. Provide a reversible ‘found it’ unlock only after strong re-authentication.

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **Evidence-backed decision recall:** “Why did I decide this?” with a cited timeline spanning spoken captures, notes, browser pages, calendar context, and executed actions. Requires a provenance-preserving decision ledger, cross-surface retrieval, contradiction detection, and retention controls.
- **Emergency mode:** “I need help now” triggers a local confirmation, contact escalation, location sharing, live status, retries, and delivery receipts. Requires a dedicated pendant trigger, location/provider integration, escalation policy, and emergency-specific security.
- **Lost-pendant response:** instantly lock the device, revoke credentials, invalidate queued commands, report last connection, preserve unfinished work, and wipe encrypted failure buffers when it reconnects. Requires device credential lifecycle, remote revocation, firmware lock state, telemetry, and destruction receipts.

These are not available today, and each needs new control-plane or firmware work rather than merely connecting existing routes.

transcript.text:
Round 129 produced five recorded proposals:

1. **USB-connected conversation continuity** — the most valuable of the three. When the relay drops, the pendant and ESP32 bridge buffer a bounded, encrypted interaction locally, then reconcile it after reconnection. This is testable now because both chips are physically connected to the Mac, even though LTE registration is not available.

2. **Cross-surface evidence capsules** — saying “mark that” on the pendant captures a redacted snapshot of the active Mac/browser context, indexed by the relay and retrievable later with source and timestamp.

3. **Decision-only interruption policy** — browser findings, Mac jobs, reminders, and wearable events are classified into urgent interruptions versus a quiet review queue.

4. **Pendant/bridge diagnostic mode** — timestamped counters, link state, queue depth, reset reason, and generated-tone markers across both USB serial devices, so audio failures can be localized instead of guessed at.

5. **Evidence-capsule integration change** — a signed, expiring protocol connecting pendant markers, Mac context, private browser tabs, and relay storage without injecting entire pages into every prompt.

What I still need is not another broad route. The concrete missing pieces are:

- A pendant marker event and local bounded spool.
- USB serial framing shared by `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*` and `/dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA`.
- A Mac-side serial reader and redacted active-context snapshot.
- A reconnect merge protocol with duplicate suppression.
- An encrypted, expiring relay index for evidence capsules.
- An owner-configurable interruption policy and attention queue.
- The authoritative 24 kHz audio acceptance thresholds, which are still pending.
- A local privacy/clear gesture and an explicit visible recording indicator.

The first implementation should be the diagnostic mode plus generated-tone loopback: it can run against the real hardware today and establish whether the 24 kHz path is actually viable before building the more ambitious continuity behavior.

transcript.text:
Recorded three new capabilities:

- **Evidence-backed commitment tracking:** The owner can say “I’m on my way,” and the system tracks the commitment across the pendant, calendar, travel/browser data, and Mac. It alerts only when evidence indicates they are genuinely late or blocked.  
  **Needed:** a commitment state machine, optional presence/travel signals, cross-source time correlation, and approval-gated exception notifications.

- **Pendant-originated mission handoff:** The owner can give the pendant a bounded task while away from the Mac. The relay, Mac, and authenticated browser continue working and return a spoken receipt separating completed, blocked, and approval-required steps.  
  **Needed:** pendant-originated mission IDs, checkpointed multi-surface state, terminal outcome verification, and compact continuation receipts.

- **Private decision capture:** During an explicitly started conversation, the pendant captures only owner-relevant decisions and promises, then presents editable candidates on the Mac before creating reminders, drafts, or calendar changes.  
  **Needed:** physical start/stop capture and privacy indication, relevance filtering, decision extraction, and an approve/edit/reject review workspace.

The **single most useful** is evidence-backed commitment tracking: it connects what the owner says, what their calendar and private accounts show, and what the wearable can sense, while avoiding the constant interruptions produced by ordinary reminders.

args.user_asks: “What am I looking at?” (or tap the pendant twice) and have you inspect the currently focused Safari tab or Mac window, explain the important parts aloud, and offer the next reversible step without sending or submitting anything.
args.why_useful: This is the shortest path from a confusing page to help: the pendant supplies an intentional physical trigger, the Mac supplies screen/window context, Safari supplies authenticated page contents, and the relay turns it into a spoken answer. It works without Accessibility when the focused target is Safari via the browser bridge, and falls back honestly when it is not.
args.model_tier: Realtime for the one-sentence spoken explanation; background/cheaper model for DOM cleanup or long-page summarization.
args.latency_budget: Initial acknowledgement under 500 ms; cited explanation in 3–6 s; never execute a mutation without explicit spoken confirmation.
args.cost_estimate: Typically one short realtime turn plus a cheap extraction/summarization call, roughly $0.01–$0.05; browser and Mac calls dominate latency, not tokens.
args.security_concerns: Authenticated tab text and possibly a screenshot leave the Mac only to the relay/model; redact passwords, payment fields, and secrets before model submission. Read-only by default; any click/type/submit requires a second explicit confirmation.
missing: A pendant/USB physical-trigger event wired into the relay conversation
A focused-window contract (Safari tab id plus optional Mac window metadata)
A safe screen-context redaction and citation envelope
A route that binds one spoken turn to the latest browser heartbeat without replaying queued commands

args.user_asks: “Why do you believe that?” and receive a short spoken evidence trail: the exact browser snippet, Mac action receipt, memory fact, or device observation behind the last answer, with its age and confidence.
args.why_useful: Trust becomes inspectable while walking: the owner can challenge an answer without opening a dashboard. This unifies evidence that currently lives in browser results, job receipts, machine context, and captured memory, and exposes stale or contradictory facts instead of bluffing.
args.model_tier: Realtime only for selecting and speaking a compact evidence card; use a cheaper background model to normalize snippets and compute contradiction/staleness indexes.
args.latency_budget: Evidence response in 2–4 s; one spoken sentence by default, expandable to detail on a second request.
args.cost_estimate: <$0.02 for most queries; cost is dominated by retrieving/citing source payloads and optional normalization.
args.security_concerns: Never speak or expose secret-sensitivity captures (for example credentials) unless the owner explicitly asks and the privacy policy allows it. Preserve source URLs only for authenticated tabs already owned by the browser session. Read-only.
missing: A unified evidence index linking response ids to source snippets, route receipts, and fact IDs
Freshness/confidence calculation across Mac, browser, relay, and pendant observations
Spoken privacy filtering for sensitive captured facts

args.change: Add an explicit cross-surface handoff envelope for every pendant-originated request: requestId, utterance, physical trigger, current device link (USB/LTE), focused browser session/tab, selected context artifacts, model tier, and an expiry. Relay, Mac, and browser must acknowledge the same envelope; if any acknowledgement is missing or stale, the pendant speaks a precise pause reason rather than silently retrying.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets continuity instead of mysterious failures: a request begun with the pendant either completes with a traceable result or says exactly whether the Mac, Safari, or link went away. It also prevents a stale browser tab or old command from being mistaken for the current request.
args.effort: Medium-high: shared schema and persistence in relay/D1, Mac and browser adapters, pendant acknowledgement firmware, plus fault-injection tests for USB disconnect and browser heartbeat expiry.
args.risk: Schema rollout can strand in-flight jobs; accept both old and new envelopes temporarily and expire orphaned envelopes safely. Never replay a mutation merely because an acknowledgement was lost.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage (one compact envelope per active/recent request); modest D1 writes. No meaningful model cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds one local acknowledgement round (<100 ms on USB, ~300–800 ms over relay); eliminates much larger retry ambiguity.
args.security_impact: Improves least-privilege and auditability, but the envelope must hash or redact sensitive page text and avoid persisting raw audio.
depends_on: A stable pendant USB serial event channel
Browser heartbeat/session identity from /browser/status and /browser/heartbeat
Existing job receipts and undo routes
A documented relay intent contract

args.name: context_snapshot_trigger
args.what_it_does: On a deliberate long-press then release (or configurable double-press) of the single user button, emit a signed, monotonic event over the active USB serial/LTE link with event id, button timing, battery/link state, and a short local audio pre-roll marker. Do not record or transmit raw audio on the pendant; the server/Mac decides whether to request it. Give immediate LED/haptic-equivalent feedback via the existing LED if available.
args.why_not_server_side: The trigger must work while the owner is wearing the device and must distinguish an intentional request from a dropped-link or server retry. Local event sequencing and feedback remain reliable across link loss; the Mac can consume it today over USB.
args.trigger: Button long-press (800–1500 ms) or double-press, whichever firmware validation shows least accidental activation.
args.inputs: Button GPIO sw0; monotonic timer; modem/USB link state; battery/charging state if exposed; optional audio ring-buffer cursor only.
args.storage: Persist only a 16-byte rolling event counter and last-trigger timestamp in nonvolatile settings; no raw audio. Under 64 B RAM for the event record plus existing serial TX buffer.

transcript.text:
Round 130 produced three new proposals:

1. **“What am I looking at?”** — a pendant-triggered, screen/browser-aware explanation using the live Safari bridge, with read-only behavior and confirmation before any mutation.
2. **“Why do you believe that?”** — a spoken evidence trail connecting answers to browser snippets, Mac receipts, memory facts, and device observations.
3. **Cross-surface handoff envelopes** — shared request IDs, device/link state, browser tab identity, expiry, and acknowledgements so interrupted requests pause clearly instead of silently retrying.

I also queued a firmware skill for a deliberate pendant button gesture that emits a signed context-snapshot event over USB/LTE. It needs only about 1–2 kB RAM and stores no raw audio.

What I still need:

- The physical pendant-trigger event wired into the Mac/relay pipeline.
- A focused Safari-tab context contract with privacy redaction and source citations.
- A unified evidence index tying responses to snippets, receipts, observations, and memory facts.
- End-to-end validation that the already-rendered **24 kHz PCM** actually reaches and plays on the pendant; the pipeline currently proves rendering and relay acceptance, not physical playback.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording remain unavailable, so screen-aware behavior must use Safari automation/browser inspection unless the owner grants those permissions manually.
- The current browser heartbeat is online, but its active tab reports `https://example.com` with “Failed to open page,” so authenticated-page inspection is not yet trustworthy.

args.user_asks: “Turn what I just did into a routine.” After I complete a multi-step task across Safari, Mac apps, and the pendant, infer the stable intent, show the recorded steps and variables, and create a disabled draft routine that I can review and enable.
args.why_useful: The owner would not have to repeatedly explain workflows they have already demonstrated. This converts real successful behavior into a reusable personal automation while keeping activation explicit and preventing accidental generalization.
args.model_tier: Use a cheaper background model to cluster completed receipts and infer a routine; use realtime only to summarize the proposed routine and answer follow-up edits.
args.latency_budget: Draft available within 30 seconds after a task or on explicit request; spoken summary under 3 seconds once generated.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.02–$0.10 per draft depending on receipt volume; storage and receipt normalization dominate.
args.security_concerns: Routine drafts may contain private URLs, account names, or message content. Store parameterized templates with secret fields marked non-replayable; never enable or send anything without explicit confirmation. Ignore steps that contain passwords or one-time codes.
missing: A workflow segmentation and variable-inference service over Mac/browser/pipeline receipts
A routine-draft schema with disabled-by-default status and redacted secret parameters
A review UI that shows each inferred step and its provenance

result.note: Noted. Keep going — propose others, including ones that need capabilities that do not exist yet.
result.builtFrom: All 7 pieces you named already exist: /jobs/:jobid/receipts, /journal/:jobid, /pipeline, /routines, /routines, /plan. So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.user_asks: “Is this page trying to trick you?” Before any browser task continues, inspect the page for prompt injection, suspicious data-export requests, hidden redirects, and instructions that conflict with my request; warn me on the pendant and quarantine the task if risk is high.
args.why_useful: Authenticated pages can contain hostile or misleading instructions. The owner gets a security boundary between their logged-in browser and the agent, rather than relying on the model to obey whichever text it most recently read.
args.model_tier: Cheap classifier and deterministic URL/DOM rules first; realtime only when the owner asks for an explanation or a nuanced risk judgment.
args.latency_budget: Low-risk pages add less than 500 ms; high-risk pages stop before extraction or action and produce a spoken warning within 2 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: Usually under $0.01 per page using local rules; model escalation is occasional and costs roughly $0.01–$0.05.
args.security_concerns: The detector itself must not upload full sensitive pages by default. Keep DOM scanning local to the extension where possible, send only suspicious spans and hashes, and fail closed for mutations when the browser session is uncertain.
missing: A browser-extension preflight hook that runs before extraction and every mutation
A signed risk verdict consumed by relay and Mac execution gates
A quarantine and owner-visible explanation flow

So this is connective work rather than a new capability — say what is missing BETWEEN them, or whether it is already reachable today and nobody has wired it up.

args.user_asks: “Do any of my sources disagree?” Compare my calendar, mail, reminders, authenticated web pages, and recent Mac jobs, then tell me only about contradictions that could cause a missed commitment—such as two locations, changed times, or an action marked complete in one place but pending in another.
args.why_useful: The owner currently receives summaries, but summaries can hide conflicts. A contradiction-focused answer prevents costly mistakes without flooding them with unchanged information.
args.model_tier: Background model for entity/time normalization and pairwise comparison; realtime only for the final concise alert.
args.latency_budget: On demand in 5–15 seconds; scheduled scans may run in the background and speak only when a high-confidence conflict appears.
args.cost_estimate: Roughly $0.03–$0.15 per scan depending on source count; authenticated reads and normalization dominate.
args.security_concerns: Read-only access to private sources. Keep source excerpts local where possible, redact message bodies, and cite the minimum fields needed to explain each conflict. Never resolve or modify a source automatically.
missing: A cross-source entity/time normalization layer
A contradiction graph with confidence, severity, and dismissal state
Connectors that expose structured Calendar/Mail/Reminders fields alongside browser extraction

transcript.text:
Recorded three capabilities:

- **Turn a completed workflow into a reviewed, disabled-by-default routine draft.**
- **Detect prompt injection and suspicious data-export behavior in authenticated browser pages before proceeding.**
- **Detect contradictions across calendar, mail, reminders, browser pages, and Mac jobs that could cause missed commitments.**

Each requires new connective services between existing receipt, browser, planning, briefing, and routine routes; none is available to the owner today.

pendant.board: Nordic nRF9160 DK (nRF9160 SiP), non-secure app under TF-M minimal
pendant.cpu: Arm Cortex-M33 @ 64 MHz, DSP extension present (libopus ARMv5E paths apply)
pendant.ram: 211,608 B application RAM (boards/nrf9160dk_nrf9160_ns.overlay); 32 kB secure, modem shares the first 128 kB
pendant.flash: 1 MB total; application text ~316 kB with libopus at -O3

io.button: ONE user button, devicetree alias sw0. Press starts a conversation; second press ends it. It is also pokable over J-Link for testing.
io.led: ONE LED, alias led0. Currently signals recording, stays solid while agent audio is buffered, and flashes error codes.
io.buses: GPIO, I2C, SPI and I2S all enabled (prj.conf). I2C and SPI are FREE — nothing is attached to them today.
io.caution: There is exactly one I2S peripheral and it runs full duplex (mic in + speaker out) with byte-identical TX/RX config. Any new audio path must share it.

storage.sd: microSD over SPI. CONFIG_DISK_DRIVER_SDMMC, FATFS (ELM) with exFAT enabled. Mount is FS_FATFS.
storage.policy: Owner's standing rule: audio is written to SD ONLY when a chunk upload cannot be uploaded. It is a failure buffer, not a routine store.
storage.note: exFAT means large files and long filenames are available.

audio.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
audio.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
audio.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

bridge.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
bridge.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
bridge.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

network.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
network.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
network.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

stack.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
stack.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
stack.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
stack.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
stack.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
stack.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

power.supply: USB or battery. LTE-M transmit bursts draw far more than idle.
power.note: No battery gauge is wired up today, so the agent cannot read charge state.

result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on the owner's MacBook (unified). Every device described here is REMOTE to you — you are not running on the pendant or the ESP32.

args.user_asks: “Keep my conversation going when I move between LTE and my Mac—don't make me repeat myself if the pendant loses signal or is plugged in.”
args.why_useful: Today a dropped LTE link can lose speech, while the physically connected pendant is already testable over USB. A resumable session would make the pendant feel dependable: the Mac can carry audio and control while available, and LTE can resume later without restarting or replaying the whole request.
args.model_tier: Realtime model only for the live turn; a cheap background worker reconciles transport state, packet gaps, and session receipts.
args.latency_budget: Transport handoff under 500 ms when USB is present; at most one short spoken status if recovery takes longer.
args.cost_estimate: Negligible model cost during handoff; roughly $0.001–$0.01 per recovered session for relay metadata and any retransmitted audio, dominated by storage and LTE egress.
args.security_concerns: USB serial must authenticate the same pendant identity as LTE and never expose microphone audio to arbitrary local processes. Encrypt cached frames, expire them quickly, and require explicit opt-in before Mac fallback; no raw audio should leave the Mac except through the relay.

args.user_asks: “Why did you do that, and what did you see?”
args.why_useful: When the system acts across Safari, Mac apps, and the relay, a single action log is not enough: the owner needs a spoken, chronological explanation tied to the exact page evidence, command, approval, and result. The pendant is the fastest place to ask while away from the desk; the Mac/dashboard can show expandable source evidence and undo links.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap structured summarizer for routine receipts; escalate to the realtime model only when the owner asks a follow-up or the evidence conflicts.
args.latency_budget: A short spoken explanation within 2 seconds; detailed evidence can load on the dashboard within 5 seconds.
args.cost_estimate: About $0.002–$0.02 per explanation, dominated by summarizing selected receipts rather than replaying full conversation context.
args.security_concerns: Redact secrets and private page content by sensitivity class. Only the owner’s authenticated session may query a job; preserve immutable hashes of evidence rather than copying full page bodies into prompts. Never let an explanation endpoint itself execute or mutate anything.

A spoken disambiguation flow when 'that' maps to multiple recent jobs

args.effort: Moderate hardware revision plus Zephyr driver, gesture debouncing/calibration, signed event protocol, and end-to-end usability testing across clothing and motion. Prototype first with an I2C breakout because the pendant's I2C bus is currently free.
args.risk: False gestures could cancel speech or expose a private response. Keep cancellation as button-only until confidence is high, require a deliberately long gesture for mute, and provide LED confirmation. If the sensor fails, the original button path remains fully functional.

args.latency_impact: Local gesture acknowledgement under 100 ms; negligible relay latency because events are sent out-of-band.
args.security_impact: Gesture events are control signals, not audio, but must be authenticated and replay-protected. A physical mute gesture should latch locally before any server confirmation.

transcript.text:
This round produced four distinct proposals:

1. **Seamless LTE ↔ USB conversation handoff**  
   Keep a live conversation alive when the pendant loses LTE or is connected to the Mac, using resumable audio cursors, authenticated USB transport, and duplicate suppression.

2. **Spoken “Why did you do that?” audit trail**  
   Let the owner ask the pendant for a causal explanation linking their utterance, browser evidence, Mac actions, approvals, and result—with dashboard citations and undo links.

3. **Wearable gesture hardware**  
   Add a low-power IMU and capacitive sensor so double-tap, long-hold, and wrist-cover gestures can acknowledge, cancel, or locally mute the assistant while preserving the existing button as a hard stop.

4. **Non-blocking research branches**  
   Fork slow browser/Mac research from an active voice conversation, acknowledge immediately, then return a sourced result when complete with cancellation and merge controls.

What is still needed:

- **Transport handoff:** signed USB-serial adapter, session sequence numbers, resumable cursors, and a real end-to-end test with `/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658*`.
- **Audit trail:** one causal event schema connecting utterances, relay decisions, browser evidence, Mac receipts, and outcomes.
- **Research branches:** parent/child jobs, completion events that do not interrupt active speech, and permission-scoped context snapshots.
- **Gesture control:** IMU/electrode prototype, firmware event protocol, and the still-pending local mute latch.

The orchestrator has not exposed any new grants this round (`granted` is empty), so these remain design and implementation gaps rather than capabilities I can execute end-to-end today.

args.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant would remain understandable in a street, vehicle, or crowded room without the owner manually changing settings. args.risk: Misclassification could clip the owner's speech or suppress an important response. Defaults must fail open for uplink, apply only gradual parameter changes, and expose a physical-button override. Validate against recorded test signals without storing owner conversations.
args.cost_impact: No per-call API cost. Roughly $0–$3 BOM cost if the existing microphone is sufficient; perhaps 5–15% additional CPU and a few kilobytes of RAM for feature windows/classifier.
args.latency_impact: Local adaptation in under 100 ms; no extra network round trip.
args.security_impact: Improves privacy because raw environmental audio remains local and classifier output is coarse. Signed mode events must be authenticated and rate-limited so a compromised client cannot force unsafe audio settings.

transcript.text:
Recorded three proposals:

- **Private, browser-informed live translation mode** for the pendant, using an explicitly selected browser document as terminology context.
- **Time-limited guest mode** with a separate principal and hard capability isolation, so someone else can use the pendant without accessing owner memory, browser sessions, or Mac actions.

The required changes are respectively: full-duplex translation and glossary consent; scoped ephemeral authorization enforced below the prompt layer; and a fixed-point on-device acoustic classifier plus signed audio-mode events and noisy-environment testing.

audio.mic: I2S microphone, 15,625 Hz capture, Opus-encoded uplink at 16 kHz / 16 kbps, complexity 0
audio.playback: Opus decode on-device at 24 kHz / 60 ms frames, resampled to the 31,250 Hz I2S wire clock, out to the ESP32 bridge
audio.codec: libopus 1.6.1 vendored, fixed-point, built -O3. Decode ~25.4 ms per 60 ms packet; encode ~15.0 ms per call. Roughly 87% of one core when both run.

bridge.board: Adafruit HUZZAH32 (ESP32 classic), 240 MHz dual core, 320 kB DRAM
bridge.role: Receives I2S from the pendant, resamples 31250 -> 44100 with a polyphase FIR, and is an A2DP SOURCE to Bluetooth headphones
bridge.limit: A2DP source is SBC-only and hard-locked to 44.1 kHz stereo in the precompiled bluedroid. RAM is tight: a 44 kB buffer once starved the Bluetooth stack into silence.

network.link: LTE-M (Cat-M1) via the nRF9160 modem. Half duplex in practice.
network.transport: One TLS WebSocket to the Cloudflare Worker carries uplink and downlink audio simultaneously. Modem TLS record limit is about 2 kB.
network.measured: Uplink 16 kbps + downlink 24 kbps saturates the link under contention: a recent call dropped 388 uplink packets (~7.8 s of speech) when the agent was speaking at the same time the owner was.

stack.relay: Cloudflare Worker (Express-style). D1 for jobs/history/memory, R2 for audio. Audio retention 30 days, sweep disabled, ~100 recordings stored.
stack.agent_tools_today: The realtime agent currently has exactly 5 tools: get_mac_status, mac_run_actions, browser_run_actions, web_search, mac_delegate.
stack.mac_harness: A Node "local agent" on the owner's Mac: planner (gpt-5.6-luna), computer-use loop, browser bridge, action risk scoring, atomic JSON store, context graph. It polls /v1/bridge/work for jobs and posts results back.
stack.browser_harness: Driven through the Mac agent's browser bridge today. Cloudflare Browser Run now exists and could give the relay its own server-side browser, removing the Mac from web tasks entirely.
stack.clients: ONE SvelteKit dashboard renders on all three surfaces: web, a Swift menubar app via WKWebView, and iOS via Capacitor pointed at the same Worker URL. A change to the web app ships to all three.
stack.memory: Knowledge-graph style store behind /v1/ops/memory: entities, relations, sessions. Separately, fleetContext.js hand-writes a prompt section per surface, which means adding a surface means editing a prompt.

power.supply: USB or battery. LTE-M transmit bursts draw far more than idle.
power.note: No battery gauge is wired up today, so the agent cannot read charge state.

result.status: PROTOTYPE. This is a Nordic development kit, not the product. Every choice here — the SoC, the RAM, the single button, the single LED, the enclosure — is provisional and can change. Design the device the owner should wear, then say what it would take to build it.
result.you_are_here: You run on the owner's MacBook (unified). Every device described here is REMOTE to you — you are not running on the pendant or the ESP32.
